articles.headline: Jacksonville Jaguars remain in the NFL hunt thanks to Foyesade Oluokun's bone-crunching efforts
articles.description: Runaway AFC South leaders the Jacksonville Jaguars continued their impressive start to the season, with Nigerian-American linebacker Foyesade Oluokun starring in a 19-17 win over the Philadelphia Eagles.
articles.body:
Runaway AFC South leaders the Jacksonville Jaguars continued their impressive start to the season, with Nigerian-American linebacker Foyesade Oluokun starring in a 19-17 win over the Philadelphia Eagles.

Week 5 was a week in which many of the best performances from players with ties to Africa came from those who ultimately narrowly ended up on losing teams.

Zimbabwe's Nate Landman (LA Rams) was up there with Oluokun for defensive impact in a 37-34 loss to the Buffalo Bills. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who has proudly repped Sierra Leone on his helmet, was another prime example of an unlucky star performer, as the Seattle Seahawks went down 32-29 to the San Francisco 49ers.

However, the Niners themselves benefitted from standout performances from two players with Nigerian ties -- Malik Mustapha and Osa Odighizuwa.

African Player of the Week: Foyesade Oluokun (Jacksonville Jaguars)

The son of Nigerian parents, Oluokun has been instrumental in the Jaguars' success so far this season -- an understated but important part in one of the league's best defenses. In week 5, he starred with 10 tackles, including six solo and one for a loss, in the win over the Eagles.

One could argue that Oluokun did not produce as many spectacular standout moments this week as the likes of Landman on defense and Smith-Njigba on offense and was fortunate to end up on the winning side when his main competitors for this week's award did not win their respective games.

However, a counter to that would be that the often unseen steady contribution that Oluokun makes week-in-week-out is probably worthy of more accolades than he gets. In a sense, this Player of the Week prize could be seen as overdue recognition for a sturdy contribution over the course of five games -- four of which have seen the Jaguars come out on the winning side.

African Moment of the Week: Jaxon Smith-Njigba (Seattle Seahawks)

Smith-Njigba -- of Sierra Leonean descent through his grandparents in a family with deep, complex West African ties -- weaved his way through four nearby Niners bodies to score a 16-yard catch-and-run touchdown off a Sam Darnold pass in the third quarter against the Niners, handing the defending Super Bowl champions the lead.

The Seahawks may eventually have gone down in a narrow fight, but their star wide receiver was impactful as usual. He tallied 118 total yards, including 102 yards across five receptions.

He did, it must be acknowledged, have a costly drop towards the end of the game. However, a bad moment towards the end of the game does not completely cancel out a memorable moment earlier - no matter how used to his brilliance we have become.

With a record of 3-2 across the first five games, the defending champions can be forgiven for showing signs of growing pains, but as long as JSN is on board and on song, they cannot be written off.

articles.headline: Why are Shakhtar playing Champions League games at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge?
articles.description: Explaining why Ukrainian side Shakhtar Donetsk will play home Champions League games at Chelsea's stadium.
articles.body:
Shakhtar Donetsk will host AEK Athens in the Champions League on Wednesday but the game will be played nearly 1,700 miles from their Ukraine home.

Stamford Bridge, Chelsea's home stadium, will act as Shakhtar's home ground for their European fixtures this season.

ESPN breaks down why that's happening...

Why are Shakhtar playing at Stamford Bridge?

Shakhtar are based in the Ukrainian city of Donetsk.

But they haven't played at their home ground, the Donbas Arena, since 2014. This year, amid security reasons due to Russia's invasion of Ukraine, they were seeking a stadium for their four home fixtures in the league phase of the Champions League.

Shakhtar have recently played 'home' European fixtures in Poland, Slovenia and Germany and were linked with using Brentford's stadium this season, but ended up agreeing to play at Stamford Bridge.

FC Shakhtar said: "Playing our Champions League home matches at Stamford Bridge is a special opportunity for Shakhtar. We are grateful to Chelsea Football Club for the opportunity to host our games at this special venue. Stamford Bridge is one of the most famous stadiums in world football, with an incredible history and atmosphere. We are convinced that Shakhtar's matches in London will provide unforgettable emotions for Ukrainian and English fans."

The 2021 UK census states that approximately 19,000 Ukraine-born people live in London.

How does it affect Chelsea?

Chelsea have no European fixtures this season after finishing 10th in the Premier League last season.

The Blues even cited their "disappointing 2025-26 season and failure to qualify for European football" as part of their reasoning to welcome Shakhtar.

A Chelsea statement said: "FC Shakhtar have played in countries across Europe and we look forward to welcoming them to London for their Champions League campaign this year.

"We will be working with the Shakhtar team closely over the coming weeks to ensure that matchdays run safely and smoothly for their team and supporters."

What matches will Stamford Bridge host?

Shakhtar vs. AEK Athens, Oct. 14

Shakhtar vs. Sporting CP, Nov. 3

Shakhtar vs. Fenerbahce, Nov. 25

Shakhtar vs. Real Madrid, Jan. 27

Chelsea were owned by Roman Abramovich

Chelsea were formerly owned by Russian oligarch Roman Abramovich.

He was forced to sell the club after 20 years in 2022 under pressure from UK government sanctions after Russia invaded Ukraine.

Where do Shakhtar play home domestic matches?

Shakhtar have largely played their 'home' matches in the Ukrainian league at the Lviv Arena, which is 600 miles from Donetsk, since 2014.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Real Madrid, Barcelona chase Spurs defender Porro
articles.description: Tottenham defender Pedro Porro is being tracked by Real Madrid and Barcelona. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Tottenham Hotspur defender Pedro Porro is being tracked by Real Madrid and Barcelona, while Liverpool have shortlisted Juventus defender Pierre Kalulu. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Tottenham Hotspur right back Pedro Porro is considering leaving the Premier League for a return to Spain, with Barcelona and Real Madrid monitoring his situation. Cadena Ser claims Madrid are leading the race, having monitored him before moving for Denzel Dumfries. Meanwhile, Sport reports that the 27-year-old, who is under contract until 2031, is also of interest to Barca, but the move is dependent on the club freeing up funds, while cheaper alternatives like Iván Fresneda are also being assessed.

- Liverpool have shortlisted Juventus defender Pierre Kalulu as a right-back target for next summer, according to Tuttomercatoweb. The Reds admire the France international's versatility alongside Roma's Wesley, though Juventus are actively working to get Kalulu to sign an improved long-term contract.

Arsenal and Aston Villa hold an advantage over Newcastle United in the pursuit of RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa due to offering Champions League football, according to Football Insider. All three clubs are tracking the 21-year-old Norway international after his impressive start to the season saw him bag seven goal contributions in seven appearances.

- Bournemouth have softened their stance and are willing to allow midfielder Alex Scott to leave in January, reports the Daily Mail. However, the Cherries will demand a fee of over £100 million for the 23-year-old's transfer and will only permit a mid-season departure if their Premier League survival remains secure.

- Manchester United, Tottenham Hotspur, and Everton are keeping tabs on Dinamo Zagreb striker Dion Beljo ahead of a potential January move, per TEAMtalk. The 24-year-old Croatia international has scored 12 goals in his last 14 games, drawing scouting interest from Brentford, Manchester City, and Chelsea as well.

Other rumors

- Chelsea, Bayern Munich, Barcelona and Real Madrid have all added Brighton central defender Luka Vušković to their transfer shortlists ahead of next summer. (Ekrem Konur)

- Viking Stavanger defender Henrik Falchener is attracting interest across Europe after Southampton had a €9.5 million bid to sign him turned down in the summer. (Sky Germany)

- Tottenham Hotspur are considering an €80 million January bid to sign Atlético Madrid midfielder Álex Baena to reinforce their attack following Xavi Simons' injury. (La Razón)

articles.headline: Walker Kessler impresses in preseason debut for Lakers
articles.description: Lakers center Walker Kessler made a strong first impression in his preseason debut Tuesday, finishing with 11 points on 4-for-6 shooting, nine rebounds, one block and one steal while playing only in the first half.
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS -- Los Angeles Lakers center Walker Kessler made a strong first impression in his preseason debut Tuesday.

The big man had 11 points on 4-for-6 shooting, nine rebounds, one block and one steal in L.A.'s 101-89 loss to the Golden State Warriors, playing only in the first half.

"I mean, it was a lot of fun being out there again," Kessler said. "It's been so long. Before the game I was actually pretty nervous, to be honest. But getting out there and just playing with the guys, it was a blast."

It had been 347 days since Kessler last appeared in an NBA game on Oct. 31 of last season for the Utah Jazz before undergoing season-ending surgery to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder in November.

After an offseason sign-and-trade to L.A., when the Lakers committed two future unprotected first-round picks and two pick swaps on top of a four-year, $130 million contract to the 25-year-old, he had to wait a little longer.

In one of the first couple of days of training camp, he jammed his left pinkie finger on the backboard while attempting to block a shot and was sidelined for the Lakers' first three preseason games.

Kessler said he was held out for "precautionary" reasons, but by playing Tuesday, he will still have the chance to play in two exhibition games (including Friday at home against the Denver Nuggets) before the regular season begins against the Warriors on Oct. 22.

His impact Tuesday was immediate. In the 16 minutes Kessler was on the court, the Lakers outscored the Warriors by 15. In the 32 minutes he wasn't, Golden State outscored L.A. by 27.

"I think I have a certain presence on the floor, but I think my teammates around me did a great job of playing defense on the perimeter," Kessler said. "I think we shared the ball really well tonight ... especially in the first half. It was a lot of fun."

Lakers coach JJ Redick praised the effort of the five-year veteran.

"I think he's a great fit for our team," Redick said. "Thought he did a nice job of running the floor, crashing, had some terrific rebounds in traffic, protected the rim. Just really, really good first half from him."

It's an effort Redick expects to see whenever Kessler is in the game.

"The word I've used with him, the challenge, is just being relentless," Redick said. "Just in terms of the motor on both ends. Running the floor, diving, screening, crashing the glass."

The message has resonated with the Lakers' new man in the middle.

"JJ and I talked, and that's kind of what we came up with this year: 'relentless,'" Kessler said. "And for me, that means just crashing every time, trying to be a presence in the paint, inside, outside, play hard, don't take plays off, on the offensive end and defensive end. So that's going to be my goal for this year."

articles.headline: Wayne Rooney: Lisandro Martinez 'disrespectful' for Man United rant
articles.description: Wayne Rooney has criticised Lisandro Martínez for his claims that Manchester United's hierarchy didn't help the players enough in the transfer window.
articles.body:
Wayne Rooney has criticised Lisandro Martínez for his claims that Manchester United's hierarchy didn't help the players enough in the transfer window.

Defender Martínez reacted explosively after United lost 2-0 to Atlético Madrid in the Champions League on Tuesday, insisting director of football Jason Wilcox should have brought more quality into the team throughout the summer.

But his interview has drawn criticism from United legend Rooney who used his own experience to explain why Martínez's public outburst was wrong.

"For me it's disrespectful to his teammates," Rooney told Amazon Prime.

"I had a similar situation when I went in and asked Sir Alex Ferguson about what players we were bringing in.

"I apologised two days later, so I can speak from experience of what he's just done.

"It is very disrespectful. There are a lot of young players in that dressing room, as well. They are looking for some guidance from experienced players."

Manager Michael Carrick has won just one of seven games this season, and United have lost three of their past five outings.

But Martínez spared Carrick from his criticism and instead aimed his words at the executives of the club.

"It is a reflection of the mirror of how is our club at the moment," Martínez told Amazon Prime in Madrid. "We did a fantastic season last season and now we expect more from the top, more players to compete because many teams bring many players as well.

"Atlético have an amazing team and they deserve to win today.

- Martínez exposes Man United's harsh reality: Blame lies with top brass, not Carrick

- Clarence Seedorf: I understand why Kobbie Mainoo is compared to me

- Man United could never contend for the Premier League title -- but they aren't so bad either

"But I expect more [investment]. 100%. I expect more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox]. I have to be honest, as players we have to do more, but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night."

Martínez insisted that criticism shouldn't head in Carrick's direction because regularly changing the manager would not solve United's problems.

The Argentina defender insisted that United didn't do enough to evolve their squad from last season.

Carrick refused to be drawn on Martínez's claims when he was asked.

articles.headline: Tyreek Hill found liable for 2 of 10 counts in battery trial; wife awarded $500K
articles.description: A Miami jury returned a mixed verdict in the assault and battery civil trial against Tyreek Hill, finding the former NFL receiver liable for two counts of battery but not liable for the eight other claims made by his estranged wife, Lakeeta Vaccaro.
articles.headlineJa: タイリーク・ヒル、暴行裁判で10項目のうち2項目の責任を認められる。妻に50万ドルの賠償金支払い命令
articles.descriptionJa: マイアミの陪審員は、タイリーク・ヒルに対する暴行の民事裁判において、元NFLレシーバーのヒルに2件の暴行罪の責任があるとする一方、別居中の妻ラキータ・バカロによる他の8件の主張については責任を認めないという評決を下した。
articles.body:
MIAMI -- A jury on Tuesday returned a mixed verdict in the assault and battery civil trial against Tyreek Hill, finding the former NFL wide receiver liable for two counts of battery but not liable for the eight remaining claims made by his estranged wife, Lakeeta Vaccaro. 

The jury awarded Vaccaro $500,000 in compensatory damages but denied her claims for punitive damages.

A relieved-looking Hill hugged one of his attorneys, Christi Bright, as the verdict was read. Hill smiled and shook his lawyers' hands as he left the courtroom.

"Mr. Hill was very pleased that he was able to get his story out and to be able to tell the world what he's not been able to speak about," Bright told reporters. "He's very grateful."

The six-person jury, along with two alternates, ranged in age from 29 to 57 and consisted of five men and three women. They reached the verdict after nearly four hours of deliberation.

The weeklong civil trial involved multiple allegations of physical and verbal abuse committed by Hill toward Vaccaro. 

Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, told a local news station that Hill's current playing situation is "fluid" and "a deal could happen any time." An NFL spokesperson told ESPN last week that Vaccaro's allegations against Hill remain "under review of the personal conduct policy."

During closing arguments, Vaccaro's lawyer, Paul Schwiep, told the jury "her account is consistent and it's corroborated by contemporaneous evidence."

Schwiep asked the jury to "restore her dignity" by awarding her compensatory damages in the amount of $8 million. 

"Money doesn't undo the harm, but it's just how our civil justice system works," Schwiep said.

Hill's attorney Michael Gottlieb told jurors during closing arguments this lawsuit is "all about money and divorce," and that the allegations of abuse arose only after Vaccaro lost a claim for additional spousal support.

"Her ambition to take his money wasn't met. So she files this action," Gottlieb said.

Vaccaro testified in court that the abuse started on Jan. 11, 2024, when the couple began arguing over a postnuptial agreement. Vaccaro told jurors Hill grabbed a necklace off her neck, put his hands around her neck and grabbed and twisted her breasts.

She took a photo of markings on her chest and said the incident "terrified" her. Vaccaro texted her mother the next day, describing aspects of the fight. The texts were among multiple exhibits entered into evidence to help corroborate her account.

The jury determined that Hill was liable for that event.

Hill filed for divorce that same month but withdrew the petition shortly after, and the couple began couples therapy, according to court testimony.

A pivotal moment in the trial came when Vaccaro's lawyers played nanny camera video from an April 2025 event for the jurors. Hill and Vaccaro are heard yelling and cursing at each other. At one point Vaccaro is heard pleading with Hill to "stop."

articles.headline: Niners LB Dre Greenlaw's appeal of suspension rejected, will sit vs. Commanders
articles.description: Niners linebacker Dre Greenlaw will serve his one-game suspension in Monday night's game against the Commanders after the NFL denied his appeal Tuesday.
articles.headlineJa: 49ersのLBドレ・グリーンロウ、出場停止への異議申し立てが棄却。コマンダーズ戦は欠場へ
articles.descriptionJa: NFLが火曜日に異議申し立てを却下したため、49ersのラインバッカー、ドレ・グリーンロウは月曜夜のコマンダーズ戦で1試合の出場停止処分を受けることになる。
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- San Francisco 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw's appeal of a one-game suspension for unsportsmanlike conduct was denied Tuesday.

The suspension was upheld by hearing officer James Thrash, who was jointly appointed by the NFL and NFLPA. Greenlaw will sit out Monday night's game against the Washington Commanders and is eligible to return to the active roster the next day.

Greenlaw was suspended for a sideline dustup with multiple Seattle Seahawks during the Niners' 32-29 win on Sunday. With 6:30 left in the first half, Greenlaw hit Seattle quarterback Sam Darnold late and out of bounds, then was involved in a skirmish in which he head-butted linebacker Ernest Jones IV, who was not wearing a helmet.

The league's statement Monday said Greenlaw violated Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1 of the NFL's rules, which applies to "any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship."

Greenlaw will serve his second one-game suspension in as many years. As a member of the Denver Broncos last season, Greenlaw received a one-game suspension for unsportsmanlike conduct when he ran toward referee Brad Allen during a game and, according to the ruling, "verbally threatened him."

Rookie Jaden Dugger, who filled in for Greenlaw against the Seahawks, is likely to start in Greenlaw's place Monday night.

articles.headline: Panthers RT Moton coughed up blood before clot diagnosis
articles.description: Carolina Panthers right tackle Taylor Moton, 32, told reporters Tuesday that he coughed up blood before being diagnosed with multiple blood clots in June, an ailment that sidelined him through training camp and into the second month of the regular season.
articles.headlineJa: パンサーズのRTモートン、血栓診断前に喀血していたことを明かす
articles.descriptionJa: キャロライナ・パンサーズのライトタックル、テイラー・モートン（32歳）は火曜日、6月に複数の血栓と診断される前に血を吐いていたことを記者団に語った。この疾患により、彼はトレーニングキャンプからレギュラーシーズン2ヶ月目まで戦列を離れていた。
articles.body:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- Carolina Panthers right tackle Taylor Moton said Tuesday that he coughed up blood before being diagnosed with multiple blood clots in late June. The ailment sidelined him throughout training camp and preseason, and well into the second month of the regular season.

Moton, the longest tenured nonspecialist in Carolina, participated in his first padded practice of 2026 on Tuesday after the Panthers activated his 21-day practice window on the non-football injury (NFI) list. Moton's early season stand-in, first-round pick Monroe Freeling, worked with a trainer off to the side because of a knee injury.

Following practice, during his first conversation with reporters since OTAs, Moton detailed his illness and the steps he took to get back onto the field. Moton said upon returning from a youth football camp in Lansing, Michigan, he experienced symptoms that would eventually lead to the discovery of multiple blood clots in his right lung.

"I started coughing up blood -- and it was like a lot of it," Moton said. "And I could start feeling it leaking through my chest even -- something like really different. So, after 15-or-something minutes, I was like 'Yeah, I've got to go to the hospital.' Went to the hospital, they were doing CT scans, ultrasounds, trying to find what was going on. And that's when they found a multitude of clots in my right lung. ... So from there, they put me on blood thinners, and other than that I was just working. I just couldn't have contact on the blood thinners cause having contact on blood thinners can lead to like a brain bleed ... but ultimately doing everything I could to just work and simulate football without the contact up until then."

Moton said he felt as if his chest were congested, but he soon realized the discomfort was more than just typical congestion when he started tasting blood in his mouth. Moton said doctors aren't sure what caused the ailment, but the 32-year-old lineman is more concerned about future prevention. He was told staying hydrated is part of that prevention, as well as moving around when he travels.

Moton has traveled with the team only once this year, as he went to Jacksonville, Florida, for the Panthers' training camp joint practice and preseason game against the Jaguars. He has been consulting with a bloodwork specialist to be prepared for the weeks ahead, including Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Eagles in Philadelphia.

Moton said he was grateful to get back to work on the practice field with his teammates. He had to weigh the risk-reward factor of such a move earlier this summer.

"Ultimately, I had to just weigh the pros and cons of getting off the blood thinners, and then being able to play ball and the chance of it happening [again]," Moton said. "The chances [of a recurrence] are relatively low right now, after being on the blood thinners for three months."

articles.headline: Arsenal showed strength in depth in Lille win, but Gyökeres is a concern
articles.description: Arsenal's substitutes made the difference once again, but Mikel Arteta's side still have questions as tougher tests await.
articles.body:
LONDON -- If Arsenal's starters don't get you, the finishers probably will.

Lille were firmly in Tuesday's UEFA Champions League game for an hour or so and then a three-goal blitz in seven minutes settled things emphatically.

There were similarities here to last weekend's 2-1 win in the Premier League over Leeds United. The visitors were the better side, but Arteta made a triple substitution shortly after Arsenal took the lead, and his team went on to win.

Lille were not as front-footed as Leeds, but they carried a threat on the break and Arsenal were struggling to break them down until Jurriën Timber marked his first home start since March with a clever touch in the box to free himself and dink a delightful finish over Lille goalkeeper Berke Özer from a tight angle.

Bukayo Saka, Martin Ødegaard and Kai Havertz were already stripped off and ready to come on. Arteta could have thought twice about making the changes given the deadlock was broken, but he went through with it anyway.

"I'm going to do it more now," he joked afterward.

"I felt it was the right moment to do it, the way the game was panning out, the way the opponent was behaving as well, that we needed in those moments, in those spaces, different kinds of players, but that's it.

"Credit to the staff and obviously the ones that come in to create those moments."

"Is it about momentum as well? Yes, it is," he continued. The combination of the dam bursting and the fresh legs overwhelmed the Ligue 1 side to win 3-0.

Timber won the ball back before Ødegaard and Saka combined for Eberechi Eze to sidefoot the ball home for his first goal of the season. Ødegaard then found Havertz, who demonstrated his game intelligence in recognizing nobody was in a central position as he burst towards the byline, instead cutting it back for Saka to score his 19th European goal for Arsenal, more than anyone else for the club aside from Thierry Henry (42).

The Gunners continue their perfect start to the group stage ahead of next week's testing trip to Bayern Munich, where they will likely need to start better than they have done of late to ensure that record continues.

Nobody can argue with the end product -- that's nine wins from 10 matches so far this season including August's Community Shield victory over Manchester City -- but if there is an issue to be found, it is perhaps in the need for those "finishers" -- Arteta's preferred moniker for substitutes -- to be so decisive.

He made five changes here, including Viktor Gyökeres leading the line instead of Havertz, with Mikel Merino operating as a No. 10 in place of Ødegaard. Noni Madueke switched to the right to replace Saka, with Eze on the left in a remodeled front four.

The results were inconclusive. Lille combined diligent defending with energetic counter-attacking to cause Arsenal problems, most obviously when Ayase Ueda beat David Raya from inside the box, but his goal was disallowed for a tight offside call.

articles.headline: Cleveland Browns gets their close-up in first trailer for Hulu's 'The Land'
articles.description: Created by Dan Fogelman, the NFL-backed drama follows a fictional version of the Browns and premieres the day after Super Bowl LXI.
articles.body:
Even if the Cleveland Browns miss the NFL playoffs, fans will still have a chance to watch the team in February.

The Browns are the focus of Hulu's upcoming scripted drama "The Land," which released its first trailer Tuesday ahead of its Feb. 15 premiere.

Created by Dan Fogelman, whose credits include "This Is Us" and "Paradise," the series follows a fictional version of the Browns as the franchise navigates navigates challenges on and off the field.

Christopher Meloni, best known for portraying Elliot Stabler on "Law & Order: Special Victims Unit," stars as Danny Roarke, Cleveland's head coach who is tasked with reviving the struggling franchise. With his job on the line, Roarke's best shot at turning things around rests on his own son, a rookie quarterback out of Ohio State.

The fictional quarterback, Connor Roarke, already had his NFL draft moment earlier this year.

Ahead of the second day of the 2026 NFL draft in Pittsburgh, commissioner Roger Goodell took the stage to announce a surprise selection.

"With the first pick of the 2026 NFL draft, the Cleveland Browns select Connor Roarke, quarterback, Ohio State," Goodell said.

Of course, the announcement was part of filming for the series, not an actual draft selection.

Meanwhile, William H. Macy plays the Browns' owner, Hal Durkin, who faces a different kind of competition as he decides which of his two daughters will take over the franchise.

"It's about a football team, nominally the Cleveland Browns," Macy told Deadline in January. "They're brilliant scripts. They're Shakespearean. It's about football, but, oh, my lord, the plots are so profound, and I'm having the time of my life."

The cast also includes Mandy Moore, Chace Crawford, Sam Corlett, Tanner Zagarino, Chloe Bennet, Bridget Moynahan and Omar Epps.

With the NFL serving as a co-producer, the series will feature authentic league branding and access.

"The NFL is completely behind our show, so we've got complete access," Macy told Deadline. "I'm optimistic it's going to be something. And what if Cleveland starts winning? Because I think our team is going to do better."

"The Land" premieres the day after Super Bowl LXI, with its promotional tagline promising, "When the game is over, the real drama begins."

articles.headline: Broncos' Bo Nix says he needs to simplify approach, play faster amid rocky start
articles.description: Broncos quarterback Bo Nix said Tuesday he can find solutions if he can simplify his approach: "Making it simple, making things 1-2-3, and let's play fast and let's roll."
articles.body:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- Faced with the rockiest start to a season of his young career, and with the defending Super Bowl champions next on the docket Thursday night, Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix said Tuesday he can find solutions if he can simplify his approach.

"Making it simple, making things 1-2-3, and let's play fast and let's roll,'' Nix said after Tuesday's practice. "I think sometimes I can have a tendency of overanalyzing it and overthinking things, and that's when I'm not at my best. I want to have all the answers and get everything right. And it's too difficult

"But I do think I can make the game simpler and just get back to 1-2, check down, that sort of thing, and making sure my reads are good.''

After five games, Nix finds himself 24th in the league in QBR, 26th in completion percentage and 30th in completions over expectation as he comes off his second-lowest passing output in a game of his career. Nix threw for 123 yards Sunday in the Broncos' win over the Los Angeles Chargers, the third win of the season for the Broncos with a fourth-quarter comeback.

He already has more fumbles this season (five) than in either of his first two seasons and now has three sub-200 yard passing games over the first five weeks. Broncos coach Sean Payton has already removed offensive coordinator Davis Webb as the team's playcaller to take over those duties and try to spark the offense.

Payton has said it's about finding more schemed completions for Nix and "calm it down'' for the quarterback.

"Part of what we're trying to do is finding these throws ... we're always trying to find those plays that are clean and against the coverages you want,'' Payton said. "[But] it's bumpy, so we're constantly grinding to calm it down and create some matchups, and some call it first or second into the progression throws that make it less risky.

"There is that happy medium.''

The Broncos (3-2) have a short week before they face the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday night at Empower Field at Mile High.

The Seahawks have made life difficult for opposing quarterbacks this season. They lead the NFL in takeaways (11), interceptions (seven) and pass rush win rate (65.5%).

Asked about limiting turnovers, specifically against the Seahawks, in the search for big plays, Nix reaffirmed his desire to clear his head and make good decisions.

"Honestly, truly the biggest battle now,'' Nix said. "At the end of the day it's like who cares? Why would I go out there worried about throwing an interception, why would I go out there trying to throw every football 50 yards down the field? Just play the play. If the play is there hit it, if it's not there, check it down, run, throw it away, punt. Who cares?''

Asked about his own confidence level in a difficult start, Nix added: "I'm confident in my preparation, I'm confident in my coaching, I'm confident in the way we're going to structure the game to call plays. I know it's going to be there.''

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Chelsea confident in January move for Scott
articles.description: Chelsea are growing confident of signing Bournemouth's Alex Scott. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Chelsea are growing confident they will be able to sign AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott in January. Meanwhile, Barcelona and Real Madrid were at Anfield on Sunday to watch Erling Haaland when Manchester City faced Liverpool.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Chelsea are increasingly confident that they will sign AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott during the January transfer window, according to TEAMtalk. The belief is that the 23-year-old would find it difficult to turn down a move to Stamford Bridge and the Blues are willing to meet the Cherries' demands, with any deal likely to reach around £100 million. Bournemouth turned down all interest in Scott during the summer, but the England international's contract expires in 2028 and he has so far resisted any calls for an extension.

- Barcelona and Real Madrid scouts were at Anfield to scout Manchester City striker Erling Haaland as he opened the scoring in a 3-0 win over Liverpool, according to TEAMtalk. Both of the Spanish giants continue to monitor the possibility of a future move following the club's guilty verdict for hundreds of financial charges. The two clubs weren't just there to watch City players, though: Barça have also been monitoring the situation of defender Ronald Araújo, who is on loan at Liverpool, while Madrid have been checking on Liverpool midfielders Alexis Mac Allister and Florian Wirtz.

- Borussia Dortmund have been interested in U.S. youth international and Philadelphia Union striker Malik Jakupovic for some time, reports Sky Germany. In the summer, the Bundesliga club submitted an offer for the 17-year-old that was worth €2m-€3m but was ultimately rejected. Contact continues to exist but there is major competition for Jakupovic with Chelsea, RB Salzburg and Stuttgart all looking at him while Eintracht Frankfurt also have in the past.

- Chelsea will need at least £50 million to tempt Barcelona into letting midfielder Frenkie de Jong leave in the January transfer window, according to Football Insider. Chelsea are looking at the 29-year-old as they continue their efforts to replace Enzo Fernández after the Argentina international joined Manchester City in the summer. De Jong is out injured but the Dutch midfield is nearing a return to fitness, although that return could make a move more difficult for the Blues as Barça have been eagerly awaiting his return.

- Ruben Amorim wants AC Milan to sign Sassuolo midfielder Darryl Bakola, who has also received interest from Roma and Juventus, reports Calciomercato. Amorim was surprised by the 18-year-old's quality when the Rossoneri drew 1-1 against Sassuolo at Mapei Stadium, when Bakola was named man of the match. The young Frenchman is being considered by scouts across Europe, and having been signed for €10 million plus €2 million in add-ons last January, he could now command over €30 million.

articles.headline: Péter Gulácsi misses Champions League game due to armed home invasion
articles.description: Villarreal goalkeeper Péter Gulácsi missed his team's Champions League game against Napoli on Tuesday because of an armed home invasion at his house, the club said.
articles.body:
Villarreal goalkeeper Péter Gulácsi missed his team's Champions League game against Napoli on Tuesday because of an armed home invasion at his house, the club said.

Spanish media reported armed men entered the Hungarian goalkeeper's house while Gulácsi was there with his wife and their two children. It reportedly took place overnight from Monday to Tuesday.

There were no reports of injuries.

The club said before the game that the 36-year-old Gulácsi would be unavailable "due to personal reasons." Luiz Júnior was in goal for Villarreal because of Gulácsi's absence.

The Spanish club won the league-phase match 3-1.

- FIFA president Gianni Infantino received undisclosed $1.7M World Cup payment

Gulácsi is a new signing at Villarreal, having joined from RB Leipzig in August. He spent more than 10 years with the German club having had spells with Red Bull Salzburg and Liverpool prior to that.

The Hungarian has 58 caps for his country.

Information from the Associated Press contributed to this report.
